newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dead Hong Kong activist's sister seeks Japan apology.
newsitem.headline: Dead Hong Kong activist's sister seeks Japan apology.

text.p: The grieving sister of a drowned Hong Kong activist won an audience with Japanese diplomats on Wednesday after protesting outside the consulate about her brother's death, but she complained that Japan was insincere.
Activist David Chan drowned last week in the East China Sea after jumping off a ship in protest against Japan's control of disputed islands northeast of Taiwan, which are also claimed by China.

Chan Lai-ying, his eldest sister, was given an audience at Japan's Hong Kong mission after she staged a doorstep protest there on Wednesday. But she said the meeting was useless as the officials were not sincere and they refused to apologise.
"I demanded the Japanese government make a public apology," she told reporters. "They said they would give the message to Tokyo. But I did not feel they were sincere about it."

Japan has claimed the territory, a cluster of uninhabited rocky islets which it calls the Senkakus, since 1895, and refuses to say that sovereignty over the territory is up for discussion. China, which calls the islands the Diaoyu group, has claimed them for centuries.
